clue.text: Flop about pitch, obscuring right of way

indicators.note: obscuring hides the original words by jumbling their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A failed attempt to hide a pitch has blocked a path the public may use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flop about pitch' reads like a description of a mishap, but its three words together are the fodder, and 'obscuring' tells you to jumble them.
explanation.definitionFit: A path open to everyone on foot is a legal right of way in Britain.

clue.text: Work at university accepted by local area people

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a local area is a place
OP is the usual short form of opus, a work
U is short for university

explanation.surface: A piece of work done at college is welcomed by people in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general mass of ordinary people in a place.

clue.text: Objectively, I would keep old Peruvian ready to meet deadline

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: in the objective case I would be ME, giving BE ME
the inti was Peru's currency before the sol replaced it

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly says they would keep an old Peruvian coin to beat a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively' is about grammar, not fairness: in the objective case 'I' becomes 'me', so 'I would' becomes 'be me'. The inti was Peru's currency from 1985 to 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving or finishing before a cut-off point is being punctual enough to meet the deadline.

clue.text: Small island's lifting gear has top missing

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a winch is a lifting device

explanation.surface: A tiny island's crane is short of its top part.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is a Scottish word for a small island, found in many place names.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Ireland an inch is a small islet, as in Inchcolm.

clue.text: See 1
Like impractical thinker who'd roll tyre round

indicators.note: turning round suggests the letters are spun into another order

explanation.surface: A dreamer is the sort of person who would push a tyre about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like it describes the tyre, but it is the signal to rearrange WHO'D ROLL TYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with their head in higher spiritual realms is dreamy and unworldly, like an impractical thinker.

clue.text: Train Henry to swim in a sea

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective naming the sea, the Tyrrhenian Sea

indicators.note: letters set swimming drift around into a new order

explanation.surface: Coaching Henry for a swim in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrrhenian is the part of the Mediterranean west of Italy, bounded by Sardinia, Corsica and Sicily.

clue.text: Suggesting lama in Marx Brothers film

parts.note: the answer read as an instruction is a six-letter creature followed by a word meaning mad, which signals scrambling; scrambled, that creature spells the clue words lama in

explanation.surface: A clue to a Marx Brothers film is that it features a llama.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, taken as an instruction (ANIMAL gone crackers), produces the clue words LAMA IN. 'Crackers' means mad, so it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Crackers is the 1930 Marx Brothers comedy adapted from their Broadway show.

clue.text: Selassie is again defended on air, being much respected

indicators.note: broadcast on air, so it is the spoken sound that counts

parts.note: Haile Selassie was emperor of Ethiopia; Haile re-guarded means he is defended again

explanation.surface: A broadcast reports that the Ethiopian emperor is under protection once more and widely admired.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, HAILE RE-GUARDED, using Haile Selassie's first name, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thought of with great esteem is much respected.

clue.text: Fairytale character getting ready to welcome new church cleaner

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: priming is preparing
CE is the Church of England
a char is a cleaning woman

explanation.surface: A storybook hero prepares to receive the parish's new cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The handsome royal who rescues Cinderella is the stock hero of fairy stories.

clue.text: See 9
Exchanging very small talk, maintaining historic buildings

indicators.note: exchanging the usual one-letter abbreviations for very and small means those two letters swap places where they sit in the word

parts.note: conversation is talk
the stretch of talk that runs from very's letter to small's letter
that stretch once the two abbreviated letters have changed places

explanation.surface: Chatting idly while keeping old buildings in repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' is V and 'small' is S; 'Exchanging' makes those two letters in CONVERSATION swap places, so VERS becomes SERV.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation is the work of preserving heritage such as old buildings.

clue.text: Heartlessly ransacks building sites

indicators.note: without its heart means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: to loot is to ransack

explanation.surface: Someone callously plunders construction sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots of land for development are building lots.

clue.text: Side of stage for audience worth a full renovation

indicators.note: a renovation rebuilds something, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: The audience's side of the theatre deserves a complete makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre the imaginary wall between actors and spectators is the open side facing the audience.

clue.text: Angrily slam a large city's complaint

indicators.note: things done angrily are thrown about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a means one
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone furiously bangs the door over a big city's grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here is the medical sense, an illness, and salmonella is food poisoning.

clue.text: School idiot left home for right direction

parts.note: comp is short for a comprehensive school
an ass is a fool

indicators.note: one thing put for another replaces it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
in means at home

explanation.surface: A school fool went home instead of turning the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive, or comp, is a British state secondary school. PORT with IN in place of R gives POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south-east and the rest are compass points, each a direction.

clue.text: See 7
See 8
Possibly magnolia, I'm thinking, is higher back in village east of the Shire

parts.note: um is the sound of someone pausing to think

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: Bree is the village east of the Shire in The Lord of the Rings

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: higher means taller

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders whether a magnolia stands taller back in a Tolkien village.
explanation.walkthrough: Bree is the village east of the Shire in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings; 'back' means reading TALLER backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Several magnolias with large leaves arranged like spokes are called umbrella trees; 'possibly' flags an example.

clue.text: Understood this classic old language

parts.note: to have got something is to have understood it
hic is Latin, a classical language, for this

explanation.surface: Someone grasped this ancient tongue from the classics.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the extinct East Germanic tongue of the Goths, known from Wulfila's Bible.

clue.text: Tops of mosques in Riyadh require gold reflector

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of each word is its first letter

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Mosque domes in the Saudi capital need gilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass reflects light and images back.

clue.text: Tin ore smelted by colleague from the east

indicators.note: smelting melts ore down, so the letters are melted and reshaped

parts.note: an ally is a colleague

explanation.surface: A workmate processes tin ore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the East, so something done orientally comes in an eastern manner.

clue.text: Official report advances conspiracy theory, angering leaders

definitions.note: acta is plural, records of proceedings, read here as one report

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: An official document pushes a conspiracy theory that annoys people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like people angered by the theory, but it takes the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is the Latin word for the recorded proceedings or minutes of a body.

clue.text: Author puts down a dish of lentils

indicators.note: in a down clue putting a letter down moves it lower in the word

parts.note: Roald Dahl was the children's author

explanation.surface: A writer serves up a lentil dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in DAHL moves one place down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is the South Asian dish of stewed split lentils or pulses.

clue.text: Capriciously, I held child's ear and arms here

indicators.note: acting capriciously is acting on whim, so the letters fall in random order

explanation.surface: On a whim I gripped a child's ear and an arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' is not limbs but heraldic arms, the coat of arms painted on the shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of arms is displayed on an escutcheon, so it is where arms are shown.

clue.text: See 24
With these, Windows can hide death caught by the Spanish journalist

parts.note: curtains is slang for the end or death
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
los is a Spanish word for the
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A computer software tip about hiding a death caught by a Spanish reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' suggests the software, but it is just windows in a house, hidden when the drapes are drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: When the drapes are drawn across, the glass panes of a room are concealed from view.

clue.text: See 26
